# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

Run jobs on Windows runners (`windows-*` labels) under native `pwsh`. Native Windows pull-request jobs live in `ci-windows.yml` and Python pull-request jobs in `ci-python.yml`, so each PR workflow can be re-run independently; their checks feed the required `windows checks passed` and `python checks passed` verdicts, as Linux jobs in `ci.yml` feed `all checks passed`; Wine runs Windows Node on hosted Linux only in `ci-master.yml`. Python runtime CI checks Linux/Windows x64 on pull requests and Linux ARM64 plus both macOS architectures on post-merge pushes; releases retain all five targets ([platform policy](workflows/ci-master.yml)). `ci.yml`, `ci-windows.yml`, and `ci-python.yml` are pull-request-only. Post-merge platform checks, Linux/Windows self-hosted standbys, and manual runner benchmarks live in `ci-master.yml`, which listens to pushes to `master` and `develop` and to `workflow_dispatch`, not `pull_request`; separating workflow triggers keeps post-merge jobs out of PR check panels. `develop` is this repository's integration branch, so every push lane that follows `master` (`ci-master.yml`, `sandbox.yml`, `e2e.yml`, `node-addon-system.yml`, `release.yml`, `release-vendor.yml`) also follows `develop`, and production packaging and Desktop publication accept `develop` beside `master` and `dsh-v*` tags. The standbys validate the self-hosted failover targets on every `master` push, and on a `develop` push only while their platform switch is `selfhosted`, so a repository without those pools never queues them; preserve the existing per-platform switches (values `selfhosted` for the in-house standbys and `blacksmith` for Blacksmith's hosted runners) and the Dependabot hosted fallback under the `selfhosted` values ([failover runbook](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-ci-failover-runbook.md), [blacksmith failover leg note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-09-blacksmith-failover-leg.md)). The `DSH_CI_MACOS` repository variable routes the macOS CI jobs (`publisher-isolated (macos)` in `ci.yml`, `unit-darwin` in `sandbox.yml`, and the disabled `serial-macos`) to `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` when it is `selfhosted`; any other value, including unset, keeps `macos-latest`. Under `selfhosted`, a pull request reaches the Mac only when its head repository is this repository and neither its author nor the run's actor is Dependabot.

The manual [Windows packaging workflow](workflows/windows-package.yml) uses the dedicated self-hosted Windows x64 label `dsh-win-package-trial` under native `pwsh`; preserve this routing separately from the automatic CI lanes.

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` and cover pull requests into master or a `release/dsh-x.y.z` branch, so their definitions come from the base branch, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check`, which also publishes the review verdict as the check run `Policy / Reviewer Check`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on pushes to master or a release branch re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each job reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, and `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF` decides whether `Policy / Approve Check` runs and fails; while it runs, `Policy / Reviewer Check` is published whatever that mode says, with `success` when every file that needs review has one and `action_required` with the reviewers to ask otherwise. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node with the merged base commit in `BASE_SHA` and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, rejects upgrade guides added outside the root version's directory, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates.

The manual Desktop publication workflow selects the original successful `package` job attempt independently of `upload-artifact` archival status, then routes each retained build through `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` to its original machine's unique label. Keep Windows run steps on native PowerShell and Mac run steps on the default POSIX shell; shared entrypoints are Node scripts. Test and production jobs use separate `desktop-test` and `desktop-production` approval Environments after a credential-free preparation job.

`Publish Desktop · Rollout & Website` reuses the same original-machine routing and approval Environments. Its preparation reads retained metadata and initial publication evidence without revalidating package binaries; it does not create release tags. Cache-only recovery validates the prepared website approval digest and upload journal without another Environment approval. Rollout installs only publisher production dependencies in `desktop-rollout` and `website-rollout` checkouts; do not reuse the full-install publication checkouts. Both publication workflows run dependency-free preflights from `apps/desktop-publisher/src`. The required CI verdicts include isolated publisher installation checks: Linux/macOS in `ci.yml`, native Windows in `ci-windows.yml`. In `ci.yml`, a macOS publisher leg that GitHub abandons before any runner acquires it makes `all checks passed` warn instead of fail; every other publisher leg must succeed.
